minutes_text:
CITY OF GLENDALE
  BLUE RIBBON PENSION REVIEW EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
  SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES

  November 9, 2021

ROLL CALL

Present: Amirian, Bain, Michals, Molano, Finch
Staff: Doyle, Takhtalian, Martin, Hovsepian, Cerritos, Jensen, Holtzman, Soghomonyan

1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA

Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the November 9, 2021
Special Meeting of Blue Ribbon Pension Review Executive Committee was
Posted on November 8, 2021, on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall

2. MINUTES
  a. Approval of minutes from 10/11/21

Molano moves to approve the minutes.
Seconded by Michals.

Motion passes unanimously.

3. BUSINESS ITEMS
  a. Future Committee Agenda Items

Holtzman expresses that he’s been contacted by various members of the Committee
about where this is going: what are the solutions and approaches being considered. Jon
shares a list of approaches.

Holtzman notes that when Mary Beth Redding finishes her presentation at next regular
meeting, he’d like the rest of the committee ask about a full gamut of solutions.

He adds that at the following meeting, he wants someone from CalPERS to speak
about their plans, their returns and investment solutions.

Holtzman mentions that some members have asked him to explore out of the box
solutions, which he has no issue with at all, but he would like to make sure that those
folks contribute to the discussion.

  1
 Finch comments that she likes the presenters thus far, but thought the last presentation
went too long. Finch suggests that Redding give a brief recap of her last presentation at
the next meeting and then go into solutions at the next session. Finch also likes the
Q&A structure.

Holtzman suggests that the group should agree about what the cutoff is for meetings
Bain and Finch are in favor of an 8:30pm cutoff.

Michals agrees that 1.5 hours is a bit short, and that we should agree to a set
timeframe. Michals expresses an interest in finding a balance between allowing folks to
speak without constraint and keeping folks on topic. Michals thinks the ExCom should
be helping Holtzman figure out the goal of the agenda for each meeting

Molano is fine with the 2 hour limit. Molano highlights that if the City’s UAL is 6x the
budget, the number is so significant that it behooves Committee to have discussions
that will lead to practical discussions in the future. If we limit the discussions to 2 hours
then we need meetings to go beyond January. Molano would like ExCom to suggest the
time and hours needed to put the City’s pension obligations in context for the public.
Molano states that he would like to bring speakers with outside perspectives. Molano
suggests Leonard Gilroy. He also articulates some alternative approaches to the
pension obligation, including:
  Disbanding of Glendale police and fire
  Replacement with County
  Bankruptcy
  Replacement of paramedics with private enterprise

Amirian agrees with Finch’s comments about the timing of the meetings. He is open to
longer meetings, so long as they are scheduled in advance. Amirian also agrees with
Michals comments about keeping questions focused on the topics being presented on.
Amirian thinks that what we’ve been doing up to this point has been describing the
situation that we are in. He’s not sure that we need to spell out explicitly what the doom
and gloom looks like for the public. Amirian agrees with Michals that the ExCom’s
purpose is to determine what we want to accomplish so that Holtzman can create an
agenda to realize those goals. Amirian notes that he is open to moving beyond January.
He asks Holtzman to take a firmer hand when it comes to entertaining comments and
questions beyond the subject matter at hand. Amirian also notes that he witnessed a
public comment by a Committee member who represented themselves as a member of
the Committee and spoke as if they were speaking on behalf of the Committee. Amirian
believes the content and manner of expressing the content spoken was inappropriate
and counterproductive. Amirian requests some discussion next time about what
comments are appropriate outside the Committee meetings.

Holtzman agrees that the statement made was inappropriate because the statement
came across as if the speaker was speaking on behalf of the Committee.

  2
 Molano notes that Ms. Wolfson was the one who spoke, and notes that he thinks the
subject being raised was appropriate. Molano believes that Wolfson referred to the
Committee as a way of expressing that she has been studying the issues and may be
more knowledgeable of the topic as a result. Molano does not appreciate being limited
with regard to the topics that we will explore.

Holtzman notes that he doesn’t think anyone is criticizing the content of what was said,
but that no one should speak on behalf of the Committee at this time.

Molano agrees.

Bain notes that the Committee doesn’t have a lot of time and has many members, and
the Committee must allow multiple people to speak. Bain adds that the goals are not
clear and it feels like the Committee is wandering in the dark a bit. Bain would like the
report to present a workable solution.

Holtzman outlines some approaches to dealing with the City’s unfunded liability:
   Increasing employee contributions
   Additional payments to CalPERs and 115 Plans
   Pension Obligation Bonds
   Bankruptcy
   Reducing final compensation
   Withdrawing from CalPERS
   Contracting out/shrinking the workforce

Molano notes that he has seen scenarios where pension contributions have been
reduced by CalPERS, and all employee unions should know that there may be
repercussions.

Flynn notes that if cities don’t pay their bill to PERS, then the benefits can be reduced.
This can happen, but this is not something that Glendale has done.

Michals notes that rather than seeing withdrawal from PERS, or firing police and fire
and linking with County, as agenda items, he would like to see what option the City has
to pay the withdrawal cost.

Molano comments that Committee needs to address the current structure that continues
to put the City into debt.

  3
 Michals notes that he wants to stay focused and feels it’s unclear whether the
Committee has the authority to weigh in on the issue of whether we want to get out of
providing pensions entirely.

Flynn reminds the group that going into the future there will be more PEPRA
employees. By nature, it is thought to be a lower benefit and lower compensation. She
adds that the City is trying to get through the next 10 or so years, at which point more
PEPRA employees will be in the system. So, the long term picture looks better from the
standpoint of the benefit that will be offered to the PEPRA employees. She adds that
with regards to bond ratings, if they are downgraded, this does not change the debt City
pays on those bonds because City has a fixed rate on the bonds.

Holtzman comments that Committee had said it will conclude at the end of January, not
beginning of January. Holtzman suggests that they wait another few meetings before
deciding whether they need to ask Council for an extension.

Holtzman would like to spend time with Mary Beth Redding on the solutions he outlined
earlier. Holtzman would also like a presenter to come and discuss pension obligation
bonds. On the withdrawal question, Holtzman is not sure who the right person would be.
Holtzman comments that in the next session, the group can ask questions of Mary Beth
Redding. In the session after that, he would like someone from CalPERS, and then
someone to discuss pension obligation bonds and 115 plans.

Molano adds that if we are having someone from CalPERS he would like an expert
regarding how CalPERS has performed.

Michals agrees that we should have an independent review and commentary on
CalPERS.

Holtzman notes that CalPERS does not owe a fiduciary duty to local entities, there are
significant things on the legislative level that could be very useful. Holtzman asks
Molano about who has the most knowledgeable critique of CalPERS’ strategy.

Molano will follow up.

Michals would like to give staff as much time as possible to provide information
regarding what the City’s options would be for getting out of CalPERS.

Holtzman notes that the group should sharpen their questions for CalPERS.

Bain notes that plans outside of CalPERS have the option to freeze benefits and pay
off, rather than being all in or all out. He notes that legislative changes would be needed
for CalPERS to provide this option.

  4
 Amirian notes that reducing benefits can make it harder to recruit and retain good
employees.

Holtzman notes that with police it’s extraordinarily hard to recruit even with pensions.

Molano notes that the argument that reducing benefits will lead to lower recruitment and
loss of employees has not be validated.

Amirian would like to agendize an item for the next meeting to discuss how committee
members will present themselves to the public.

4. REPORTS - INFORMATION ONLY
none
5. REQUESTS FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS
none
6. ADJOURNMENT

Molano moves to adjourn
Bain seconds.

Meeting is adjourned at 3:44pm
